lessons.name: Frame Within Frame
lessons.shortDescription: Use natural or urban elements to frame your subject.
lessons.fullDescription:
Use natural or built elements to frame your main subject. Look for arches, windows, doors, or tree branches.

 Example: a person seen through a window or archway.

 Challenge: capture a photo where your subject is fully framed by a visible element.

lessons.name: Backlight (Silhouette)
lessons.shortDescription: Place your subject between you and the light source.
lessons.fullDescription:
Position your subject in front of a strong light source like the sun. This creates dramatic silhouettes or glowing outlines.

 Example: a person standing in front of a sunset.

 Challenge: create a photo where the subject is only recognizable as a silhouette.

lessons.name: Perfect Symmetry
lessons.shortDescription: Create a visually balanced symmetrical composition.
lessons.fullDescription:
Find or create symmetry in your scene. Use reflections, architecture, or natural elements.

 Example: building reflected in water or centered hallway.

 Challenge: capture a scene where left and right sides are nearly identical.

lessons.name: Rule of Thirds
lessons.shortDescription: Place your subject on key intersection points.
lessons.fullDescription:
Divide your frame into 9 equal parts and place your subject along the intersections for a balanced composition.

 Example: horizon on the lower third line or subject on the side.

 Challenge: take 3 different photos using the rule of thirds.

lessons.name: Texture & Detail
lessons.shortDescription: Reveal hidden beauty in everyday surfaces.
lessons.fullDescription:
Capture textures like wood, skin, metal, fabric, or stone. Use close-ups and directional light.

 Example: macro shot of a rough wall or wet leaf.

 Challenge: turn an ordinary object into an artistic image.

lessons.name: Long Exposure
lessons.shortDescription: Capture motion invisible to the naked eye.
lessons.fullDescription:
Use a slow shutter speed to record movement over time. Requires stability (tripod recommended).

 Example: car light trails or silky water.

 Challenge: capture visible motion trails from light or water.

lessons.name: Natural Light
lessons.shortDescription: Use sunlight as your main light source.
lessons.fullDescription:
Learn to use natural light effectively, especially during golden hour.

 Example: portrait during sunset or window light.

 Challenge: take a photo without flash using only natural light.

lessons.name: Forced Perspective
lessons.shortDescription: Create optical illusions using perspective tricks.
lessons.fullDescription:
Manipulate perspective to make objects appear larger, smaller, or closer than they really are.

 Example: holding the Eiffel Tower in your hand.

 Challenge: create a believable optical illusion.

lessons.name: Minimalism
lessons.shortDescription: Less elements = stronger visual impact.
lessons.fullDescription:
Remove all unnecessary elements from your frame. Focus on simplicity and subject isolation.

 Example: one object on a clean background.

 Challenge: create a powerful image with only one main subject.

lessons.name: Water Reflection
lessons.shortDescription: Use reflections to double your composition.
lessons.fullDescription:
Use water surfaces like puddles, lakes, or rivers to create reflections.

 Example: buildings reflected in a puddle.

 Challenge: capture a perfectly aligned reflection shot.

lessons.name: Motion Blur
lessons.shortDescription: Show movement instead of freezing it.
lessons.fullDescription:
Capture motion blur to express speed, energy, or action.

 Example: running person or moving crowd.

 Challenge: take a photo where motion is clearly visible.

lessons.name: Street Story
lessons.shortDescription: Capture real-life moments in the street.
lessons.fullDescription:
Take candid photos that tell a story about everyday life.

 Example: market scene, street vendor, or children playing.

 Challenge: tell a complete story in a single image.

lessons.name: Leading Line
lessons.shortDescription: Use lines to guide the viewer's eye toward your subject.
lessons.fullDescription:
Leading lines naturally draw attention to a specific point in your image and help create a stronger composition.

Examples: roads, railways, fences, sidewalks, bridges, rows of trees, or buildings.

Challenge: create a photo where the lines clearly lead the viewer to the main subject.

lessons.name: Negative Space
lessons.shortDescription: Use empty space to emphasize your subject.
lessons.fullDescription:
Negative space is the area around your subject. Using plenty of empty space can make a photo feel cleaner, stronger, and more impactful.

Examples: a person against the sky, a lone tree in a field, or a boat on calm water.

Challenge: make your subject occupy less than one-third of the frame.

lessons.name: Patterns
lessons.shortDescription: Find repeating shapes, colors, or objects.
lessons.fullDescription:
Patterns create visual rhythm and make photos more engaging.

Examples: windows on a building, floor tiles, rows of chairs, or stacked products.

Challenge: fill the entire frame with a repeating pattern.

lessons.name: Reflection
lessons.shortDescription: Use reflections to create unique compositions.
lessons.fullDescription:
Reflections add symmetry, depth, and visual interest.

Examples: puddles, mirrors, windows, lakes, or shiny surfaces.

Challenge: make the reflection as important as the actual subject.

lessons.name: Depth
lessons.shortDescription: Create a sense of distance in your photo.
lessons.fullDescription:
Depth makes a two-dimensional image feel more immersive.

Examples: foreground flowers, a middle-ground subject, and mountains in the background.

Challenge: include clear foreground, middle-ground, and background elements.

lessons.name: Color Contrast
lessons.shortDescription: Use contrasting colors to make your subject stand out.
lessons.fullDescription:
Strong color contrast instantly attracts attention and creates visual impact.

Examples: yellow and blue, red and green, or orange and teal.

Challenge: photograph a subject that strongly contrasts with its surroundings.

lessons.name: Golden Ratio
lessons.shortDescription: Compose using the natural flow of the Golden Ratio.
lessons.fullDescription:
The Golden Ratio is a composition technique that guides the viewer's eye through the image in a natural way.

Examples: spiraling staircases, curved roads, or naturally flowing scenes.

Challenge: place your subject near the focal point of an imaginary Golden Spiral.

lessons.name: Shadow Play
lessons.shortDescription: Use shadows as a key element of your composition.
lessons.fullDescription:
Shadows can create mystery, drama, and abstract shapes.

Examples: window shadows, tree shadows, or people casting long shadows.

Challenge: make the shadow more important than the object creating it.

lessons.name: Bokeh
lessons.shortDescription: Create a smooth blurred background.
lessons.fullDescription:
Bokeh refers to the aesthetic quality of out-of-focus areas in a photo.

Examples: portraits with blurred lights, flowers against a soft background, or city lights at night.

Challenge: keep your subject sharp while creating strong background blur.

lessons.name: Portrait Lighting
lessons.shortDescription: Use light to shape and enhance a portrait.
lessons.fullDescription:
Lighting determines the mood, depth, and quality of a portrait.

Examples: window light, side lighting, golden hour portraits, or dramatic shadows.

Challenge: use a single light source to create an interesting portrait.

lessons.name: Storytelling
lessons.shortDescription: Tell a story with a single photograph.
lessons.fullDescription:
Great photos make viewers ask questions and imagine what happened before and after the moment.

Examples: a traveler waiting for a bus, a child exploring, or a craftsman at work.

Challenge: capture a scene that communicates a clear story without words.
